summary.intent: Assess Phase 72 readiness, clean up drifted planning todos across Phases 70/71/72/73, then plan/execute/ship Phase 72, but the session pivoted to firefighting three CI regressions (web-e2e, desktop-e2e, sdk-e2e) discovered mid-flow, followed by an extended web-e2e flakiness diagnosis and stabilization effort, before resuming Phase 72 planning.
summary.outcome: Retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and updated ROADMAP source lists for Phase 72/73; fixed and merged PR #601 (FUSE seq-1 equivocation + stale DTO fields + perf optimization, validated green on all 3 desktop OSes) and PR #600 (web floor-store helper + sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency fix + 4 web-e2e timing-race fixes, validated 53/53 locally under CI-equivalent timeout regime and green on dispatched CI); resumed Phase 72 planning through research and pattern-mapping, with the planner spawn in progress at transcript end.

repo: This repo closes todos by deleting/moving them to completed/, not resolved/ — Phase 71 (#599) shipped without retiring its 8 source todos, leaving them stale in pending/

ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — must dispatch manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on workflows predating that input) to get pre-merge runtime validation
playwright.config.ts uses workers:3, fullyParallel:false, retries:0, timeout:90s (CI) — deliberate 'fix flakiness at source' philosophy, not accidental

ciFloor() helper in tests/web-e2e raises wait timeouts to a 60s floor only under CI (process.env.CI) — local runs use much tighter timeouts (15-30s), causing IPNS-gated mutation tests (batch delete/move, restore, create) to flake locally even when CI-safe

webServer.reuseExistingServer in playwright.config.ts is `!process.env.CI`, so setting CI=1 locally to get the 60s floor fights an already-running dev stack unless reuse is temporarily patched to always-true

Phase 71 (#599) was a broad DTO rename (readDescriptorRef→encryptedReadKey, rootIpnsName→shareRootIpnsName) enforced by API's forbidNonWhitelisted ValidationPipe — desktop-e2e .mts test drivers weren't updated, causing stale-field 400s independent of the actual FUSE bug

FUSE publish_with_cas_retry (crates/fuse/src/metadata.rs) is the shared CAS helper for both file and folder publish paths — has only 2 real callers, making it safe to add an optional preresolved_seq param without wide blast radius

gsd-core hook JSON files (plan:pre capability fragments) contain raw literal newlines/control characters inside string values, breaking both `jq` and standard JSON.parse — required writing a custom lenient parser script to extract fragments
GSD phase directories under .planning/phases/ need RESEARCH.md, VALIDATION.md (Nyquist, when RESEARCH has a Validation Architecture section) created before planner spawn

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on the first-publish branch gated only by 'inode cid empty' — a dropped/stale UploadComplete re-running that branch re-seals with a new CID at seq=1, tripping Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS first: NotFound→true first-publish, Found(seq)→route into publish_with_cas_retry with the resolved seq instead of skipping.

publish_with_cas_retry given an optional preresolved_seq param (Greptile P2 fix) so callers with an already-resolved sequence (e.g. content_ops.rs Found path) skip a redundant second resolve; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a conflict makes any pre-resolved value stale.

6.6.2 restore-version test had a no-op sync gate (getVersionCount()===1 is true both before and after a restore swap), giving zero wait for the restore's IPNS republish before reading editor content — replaced with expect.poll of the actual editor content.

ciFloor() helper only raises wait timeouts under CI; local runs keep short timeouts, causing IPNS-gated batch tests (4.10, 4.11) to flake locally on healthy/warm stacks purely due to timeout miscalibration, not real bugs.

workflow: When a background CI job doesn't run on PRs, use workflow_dispatch against the feature branch ref to get pre-merge runtime proof instead of merging blind

When diagnosing flaky tests, distinguish 'stale/no-op sync gate' (needs a real wait) from 'timeout miscalibration' (needs the same floor as an equivalent path) from 'cumulative budget overflow' (needs a higher test-level timeout) — each requires a different fix class

To verify local test fixes match what CI actually enforces, run under CI's exact timeout regime (CI=1) rather than local defaults, since divergent local/CI timeout floors otherwise cause endless whack-a-mole across unrelated tests

Rebase a PR branch onto main before dispatching a full validation CI run when a sibling PR touching shared code (e.g. Rust FUSE crate for a desktop-e2e job) has merged in the meantime, so the dispatched run reflects real merge state

friction: Chasing local web-e2e verification took 7 sequential runs (~70+ minutes) because each run hit a different ambient IPNS-timing flake (4.10, then 4.11, then 2.1 twice) before ever reaching the actual target tests (6.6.2, 8.2), due to local timeouts being tighter than CI's ciFloor-raised timeouts
Setting CI=1 locally to get the correct timeout floor broke webServer.reuseExistingServer, requiring a temporary (reverted) playwright.config.ts patch to force server reuse
gsd-core hook JSON is not valid JSON (raw control characters in string values) — jq and JSON.parse both failed, requiring a custom lenient parser script mid-session

AskUserQuestion was answered with a clarifying question back from the user ('is there anything that needs to be clarified...') rather than a direct choice, requiring the assistant to actually read all 9 Phase 72 todos to answer definitively
gh workflow run -f ref=<branch> returned HTTP 422 'Unexpected inputs' because main's workflow definition predated the ref input — had to use --ref instead
git commit hung at 2 minutes during lint-staged, apparently due to a 1Password SSH signing prompt (known issue) — had to verify out-of-band whether the commit actually landed
